Supplier: if T: X -> Y is compact and A: W -> X, B: Y -> Z are bounded linear, then TA and BT are compact. Consumer's Definition: 'it is a two-sided ideal: if K is compact and A,B are bounded then AK and KB are compact'; this is the supplier's statement with T = K and the bounded factors on either side, so K(X) is a two-sided ideal and the quotient multiplication is well defined.

Supplier: the compact operators X -> Y form a linear subspace of B(X,Y) (the zero operator is compact; sums and scalar multiples of compact operators are compact). Supplier: under the Axiom of Countable Choice, if X is normed, Y Banach and T_n: X -> Y are compact with ||T_n - T|| -> 0 for a bounded T, then T is compact. Consumer's Definition: 'it is closed in the operator norm: a norm limit of compact operators is compact ([[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]], which is stated under Countable Choice and requires the target to be Banach, as here)'; X is a Banach space and the Definition assumes Countable Choice, so the hypotheses match exactly, making K(X) closed.
